newsitem.title: USA: Williams, PBS in business education joint venture.
newsitem.headline: Williams, PBS in business education joint venture.

text.p: Williams Cos. Inc., a natural gas pipeline group with a large telecommunications network, has formed a joint venture with the Public Broadcasting System to provide business education on desktop computers, the corporations said Thursday.

The venture, called "The Business Channel, LLC, will use Internet, video-on-demand, fiber-optic and satellite technologies to bring professional development and training services to businesses, they said.

"The Business Channel helps answer corporate America's need to provide easily accessible continuing education to employees at all levels, which will be essential if they are to stay at the top of their fields in our rapidly changing world," Williams Chairman Keith Bailey said in a statement.

The 20-year agreement builds on PBS's satellite-based Business Channel set up in 1989 which already provides business programming to 6,000 companies, nonprofit institutions, colleges and government agencies.
The Massachusetts Institute of Technology has agreed to make its faculty available to American business leaders on The Business Channel in MIT's first telecommunications alliance.
Williams will invest about $20 million to expand the Business Channel's business-oriented programming, live seminars, video conferences and other educational resources.

The venture will also benefit from Williams' training subsidiary, Williams Learning Network Inc., which has the nation's largest CD-ROM and computer-based library of training materials for the chemical, refining, utility and manufacturing industries, the corporations said.

A management committee will be formed to operate the new enterprise. PBS will have sole and exclusive editorial control of all Business Channel programming and will be responsible for the day-to-day management of programming and marketing activities.

The WilTech Group, Inc., a Williams subsidiary, will provide transmission, archive and software services. Each partner will receive a 50 percent share of the gross cash flow, with PBS using its share to support public television's varied noncommercial, educational mission, they said.

PBS's 345 member stations will be invited to serve as local marketers of The Business Channel to area businesses, colleges and other organisations. There will also be opportunities for PBS stations to produce programming and other materials for the service.
By July 1, 1997, the corporations said timely, convenient and cost-effective video-based education will be delivered on-demand to an employee's computer desktop or a company's training centre.
Industry sources said the services could save employers substantial sums in travel expenses and labour by making training much more accessible at worksites.
Sun Microsystems will supply technology to the enterprise.
Williams operates an extensive system of fiber optic cables and will use the cables to deliver a wide array of training and educational programmes to businesses.
PBS, based in Alexandria, Va., is a private, nonprofit corporation, owned and operated by the nation's 345 public television stations.
Tulsa, Okla.-based Williams stock rose 37.5 cents to $51.50 on the New York Stock Exchange in early afternoon trading.
